title: 2026-06-03-legal-intake-sourcing-committee-orientation
summary: Intro to Redwood onboarding, procurement gating overview for MSA/DPA/SLA approvals; discussed data residency, KMS, SSO, pricing threshold to trigger sourcing committee; agreed to circulate redlines and scorecard; pilot proposal of 2-week smoke test. Next steps captured.
topics: Pricing approval thresholds and sourcing committee process
next_steps: Redwood to send MSA/DPA redlines by 2026-06-08
Helix to share vendor scorecard template and procurement thresholds by 2026-06-07
SE to schedule a 2-week pilot kickoff for 2026-06-15
Security to request encryption and KMS architecture diagram by 2026-06-10
action_items: Alex Rivera: Prepare and send annotated MSA/DPA redline PDF - due 2026-06-08
Priya Shah: Provide pilot runbook and benchmark plan - due 2026-06-12
Marcus Lee: Create billing example with committed vs burst pricing - due 2026-06-09
Oliver Grant (Helix): Return initial redline comments/flags - due 2026-06-11
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Rivera: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE for Helix. we've got Priya our SE, Marcus on CSM — quick intros?
[00:00:12] Samantha Chen: Hi, Sam Chen, procurement — I've got Oliver our counsel and Ravi from security, Nora from product here too. thanks.
[00:00:22] Priya Shah: Hi all, SE Priya. we'll focus on technical gating items that procurement will care about—SLA, data residency, keys.
[00:00:35] Oliver Grant: Quick ask up front — we want to understand the path to approval internally. Helix has a sourcing committee that kicks in at vendor TCV above $250k and any SaaS with data residency obligations triggers legal review. we want to align.
[00:00:50] Alex Rivera: Totally. today is orientation for that process — figure out who needs what and timeline. we'll also surface the MSA/DPA redline approach and propose a short pilot so you can validate performance and controls.
[00:01:05] Ravi Patel: On security, primary concerns: KMS integration, customer-managed keys or HSM options, audit logs, encryption in transit + at rest, and whether Redwood supports private VPC deployments. also SSO — we use SAML via Okta.
[00:01:21] Priya Shah: Redwood supports both hosted and private deployment modes. For Private we offer a VPC package and can integrate with KMS providers — we do have HSM options for some enterprise customers, and our log pipeline can export audit logs to your SIEM. small caveat — certain HSM integrations require additional lead time for key exchange.
[00:01:39] Nora Williams: When you say "hosted" — is data retained for training? that's an internal legal checkbox for us.
[00:01:45] Alex Rivera: Short answer is no by default for hosted customers who opt-out; we provide data processing terms in the DPA where we commit not to use data for training. we'll share the DPA language. there are different retention policies depending on Dedicated and Private options.
[00:01:58] Oliver Grant: We need explicit clause for no model training and also audit rights for redwood's subprocessors. can you provide subprocessors list and SOC 2 scope?
[00:02:08] Marcus Lee: We have SOC 2 Type II and can share the report under NDA. subprocessors list is maintained in the security pack; we'll drop links in the follow-up.
[00:02:17] Samantha Chen: procurement question — pricing. Helix has a preferred path: if expected annual spend < $50k, procurement can approve. 50–250k needs sourcing committee approval, >250k needs executive signoff. how do you recommend packaging for a pilot?
[00:02:33] Alex Rivera: For pilots we typically propose a fixed-cost POC — e.g., a two-week smoke test with capped consumption. we'll provide an estimate and a billing example: you can treat it as billable credit or one-off invoice. That keeps it below committee thresholds while enabling performance validation.
[00:02:50] Priya Shah: From the SE side, pilot scope: two inference endpoints, 50k tokens/day synthetic load, success criteria: latency p95 under 260ms and mean token cost within target. we'll include a runbook for load and telemetry hooks.
[00:03:06] Devin Ortiz: How do you handle fallbacks? if latency spikes do you tier to a cheaper model automatically? our ops team wants deterministic behavior.
[00:03:13] Priya Shah: You can configure routing policies: prioritize latency, cost, or region. for pilot we'll set a strict latency-first policy with alerts to ops. automated fallback happens only if you opt in — we don't silently swap without config.
[00:03:25] Oliver Grant: On MSA redlines — our legal template requires indemnity cap adjustments and narrower data definitions. we prefer a mutual indemnity and a 12-month limitation on consequential damages. are those typical negotiations?
[00:03:36] Alex Rivera: We see that a lot. Redwood's standard MSA has vendor-friendly limits but we're used to negotiating mutual indemnity and carving out data obligations. we'll mark those as high-priority items in the redline.
[00:03:47] Ravi Patel: Quick technical detail — do you support BYOK (bring your own key) for model encryption at rest? and, can keys be rotated without service interruption?
[00:03:57] Priya Shah: BYOK is available on Private deployments. key rotation is supported with rolling rekey procedures; we'd detail the timeline in the keystore integration doc. small caveat: rotation windows might add short-lived cache invalidations for active KV caches.
[00:04:13] Nora Williams: Data residency — we have EU and US customers. Some data must remain in EU. can you guarantee region pinning for model inference?
[00:04:21] Alex Rivera: Yes — region pinning is supported. for hosted we have regional pages; for Dedicated/Private you can deploy to an EU-only pool and ensure data never leaves that jurisdiction.
[00:04:32] Samantha Chen: Procurement process wise, we need: 1) draft MSA/DPA redline 2) security pack (SOC 2, penetration test summary, subprocessors) 3) pricing example and pilot SOW. once we have these, we can pre-score and see if sourcing committee is required.
[00:04:46] Alex Rivera: Agreed. we'll package those items. can I confirm dates? we propose to send redline + security pack by COB 2026-06-08 and pilot runbook by 2026-06-12.
[00:04:58] Oliver Grant: That timeline works. also regarding DPA — we need to see specific data processing sub-processor flow and an option for more restrictive transfer mechanisms (SCCs).
[00:05:08] Marcus Lee: We'll include SCC references and the subprocessors list. the DPA has an option toggle for SCCs and standard contractual clauses when needed.
[00:05:16] Samantha Chen: One other procurement wrinkle: we prefer Net 45 payment terms for pilots under $50k; anything longer needs finance approval. can you accept that?
[00:05:24] Alex Rivera: For pilot invoices we can generally offer Net 30 or Net 45 depending on deal team approval. Marcus will follow up with a billing example showing Net 30 and extended Net 45 options.
[00:05:34] Priya Shah: On the technical acceptance criteria, we'll instrument traces for token-level latency and provide a token-cost calculator for you to run scenarios.
[00:05:43] Ravi Patel: For the security pack, can you provide evidence of penetration tests from the last 12 months and an incident response playbook? we need to show the sourcing committee an IR plan.
[00:05:52] Alex Rivera: Yes, last pen test summary and IR playbook will be included. for full SOC 2 we'll require an NDA; we'll attach the process to the follow-up email.
[00:06:02] Nora Williams: Is there a standard escrow mechanism or export of logs? our compliance team asks for retained logs for 12 months.
[00:06:09] Priya Shah: Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM and retained per your policy if you choose Dedicated or Private. Hosted retention defaults are shorter but configurable via add-on.
[00:06:20] Samantha Chen: Great. can we also get a simple vendor scorecard? our sourcing committee uses a 1–5 rubric for security, reliability, cost, and support. if you can pre-populate that, it helps speed review.
[00:06:30] Alex Rivera: We'll pre-populate a scorecard and include notes. Marcus will attach the billing examples and typical SLA table — uptime targets, response times, and credits.
[00:06:41] Devin Ortiz: For SLA credits — how are they applied? is it automatic or requires a claim?
[00:06:47] Marcus Lee: SLA credits require a claim but we have an automated reporting pipeline that pre-fills the claim data; mostly it's a formal request process. credits are applied pro rata to invoices.
[00:06:58] Oliver Grant: Can you confirm indemnity carve-outs for third-party claims due to customer data?
[00:07:04] Alex Rivera: We'll propose mutual indemnity with carve-outs and specifically defined customer data responsibilities in the DPA. we'll flag that in redlines.
[00:07:12] Samantha Chen: timeline check: if we get materials by 6/8, sourcing committee meets 6/12, we need a final commercial sign off by 6/20 ideally. is that realistic for Redwood?
[00:07:22] Alex Rivera: Yes, assuming redlines are straightforward. if heavy negotiation happens it could slip. our plan: get aligned on pilot first so procurement can move forward with a smaller commitment.
[00:07:33] Oliver Grant: We'll start internal redline review immediately after you send. also cc our external counsel if needed.
[00:07:38] Alex Rivera: Absolutely — we'll include a tracked PDF and a plain text summary of the major risk items.
[00:07:45] Priya Shah: Quick note on benchmarks — we'll include a reproducible script and telemetry endpoints so your infra team can run the tests in your environment.
[00:07:53] Nora Williams: sounds good. any dependencies on our side for the pilot?
[00:07:57] Priya Shah: Primarily an API key and a set of sample prompts; if you want VPC, then network configuration and one-time setup. for hosted pilot no VPC required.
[00:08:06] Samantha Chen: we'll aim for hosted pilot first to shorten procurement friction.
[00:08:09] Alex Rivera: Good plan. Okay let's summarize — action items: Redwood to send MSA/DPA redline, security pack, pre-populated vendor scorecard, pilot runbook, and billing example by dates above. Helix to return redline comments and sourcing thresholds.
[00:08:26] Oliver Grant: Confirmed. we'll also identify if sourcing committee needs an in-person or recorded briefing.
[00:08:33] Marcus Lee: We can provide a 20-minute recorded exec summary tailored for the committee if that helps.
[00:08:39] Samantha Chen: that would be helpful.
[00:08:41] Alex Rivera: Great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the email and attachments.
[00:08:46] Samantha Chen: Thanks, bye.
[00:08:48] Everyone: Bye.
